answer: Temporal Entropy Challenge Nodes prove uniqueness by solving dynamic puzzles bound to unpredictable block hashes mined across the global network, like weather shifting across a frozen tundra. Before responding, an agent must hash its private state with this fresh seed, a process as rare and costly as finding a single pearl in deep water. Attackers cannot precompute these proofs. To fake multiple identities, an adversary must whisper massive computational power continuously into every parallel thread, paying a heavy CPU tax and severe latency penalty for each forged instance.
